approaches.name: MPFB system assets pack (makehuman_system_assets_cc0.zip)
approaches.description: Acquire the official CC0 makehuman_system_assets pack (267 MB zip, files.makehumancommunity.org), install as an MPFB pack, then fit its bundled eye .mhclo via HumanService.add_mhclo_asset(..., asset_type='eyes', material_type='PROCEDURAL_EYES') and drive with the shipped procedural_eyes.json shader.
approaches.d1Compliance: HIGH - MPFB's own geometry through MPFB's own services; zero hand-authored geometry
approaches.preStripFeasibility: REQUIRED - the pack eyes are the same MakeHuman default eyes whose .mhclo refs are all >= 13380; fit must run before the #318 strip
approaches.licence: MEDIUM - pack page declares CC0 but the brief demands 'read the .mhclo header not the pack page'; 267 MB acquisition needs a licence sweep of every staged file; pack installation needs MPFB pack-metadata JSON plumbing
approaches.gazeDrivability: HIGH (expected) - eyes fit to the socket inherit weights via MPFB's interpolate_weights / set_up_rigging; shipped body socket verts already carry eyeL/eyeR weights (31/30 verts measured), so the projection should bind eyeL/eyeR
approaches.effort: HIGH - 267 MB download, pack install plumbing (pack metadata json), whole-pack licence sweep, verify asset matches upstream
approaches.risk: pack source/host reliability; licence verified at pack level not header level; the pack is 1000x larger than the asset needed

approaches.name: Procedural spheres at the helper volumes
approaches.description: Generate parametric eyeballs positioned/scaled from helper-l-eye/helper-r-eye before the strip; weight directly to joint-l-eye/joint-r-eye; material from procedural_eyes.json. In-tree precedent: add_mpfb2_eye_rig.py (cagematch stage for the Anny rail).
approaches.d1Compliance: LOW-MEDIUM - closest to hand-authoring; 'a sphere is not an eye' (sclera/iris/cornea layering is what the shader expects); D1 says wire proven tools, never hand-author geometry. The in-tree precedent is a CAGEMATCH stage explicitly not shipped
approaches.preStripFeasibility: POSSIBLE pre-strip (helper volumes) OR post-strip (eye bone head positions survive the strip) - most flexible
approaches.licence: HIGH - no acquisition, no licence question
approaches.gazeDrivability: HIGH - direct weighting to eyeL/eyeR by construction
approaches.effort: LOW-MEDIUM - no acquisition; but geometry + material authoring and no vendor eye shape
approaches.risk: D1 tension is the disqualifier per the brief's own first criterion; fidelity of a sphere as an eye is low

approaches.name: MakeHuman upstream default eyes, scoped acquisition, fitted pre-strip through the already-proven in-tree fit path
approaches.description: The MPFB 'system assets' eyes ARE MakeHuman's default eyes, released CC0 in September 2020 and present in the makehumancommunity/makehuman2 repo at data/eyes/hm08/{low-poly,high-poly}/*.mhclo + *.obj (basemesh hm08). The .mhclo header IS the licence: 'This asset was explicitly released as CC0 in september 2020' with named copyright holders (Data Collection AB, Joel Palmius, Jonas Hauquier) - read directly, satisfying the brief's 'read the .mhclo header not the pack page'. Acquire ONLY the ~150 KB eye pair, stage in .openclinxr-local/provider-cache, fit pre-strip with the exact proven path the materializer already uses for the t-shirt/cargo-pants/toigo-flats (import_obj + apply_object_transforms + ClothesService.fit_clothes_to_human + transfer_weights_body_to_garment k-NN), material via MPFB's own PROCEDURAL_EYES path (procedural_eyes.json + eye_settings.default.json).
approaches.d1Compliance: HIGH - real vendor eye geometry (not a sphere) fitted by MPFB's own ClothesService + the k-NN weight projection already proven on this rail for three garment channels; zero hand-authored geometry
approaches.preStripFeasibility: REQUIRED and deterministic - the .mhclo vert refs 14598-14741 only exist pre-strip; the materializer already has an ordered pre-strip slot (after add_standard_rig / face keys, before the strip)
approaches.licence: HIGH - CC0 verified IN THE ASSET HEADER itself (not a pack page), with copyright holders; identical licence text in low-poly and high-poly .mhclo; brown.mhmat included
approaches.gazeDrivability: HIGH (expected, verified empirically this slice) - k-NN body-group projection transfers the socket body verts' eyeL/eyeR weights (31/30 measured on the shipped body) onto the eye mesh
approaches.effort: LOW-MEDIUM - ~150 KB scoped download; no pack install plumbing; reuses in-tree proven functions
approaches.risk: the fit must run pre-strip (order is load-bearing); low-poly eye at 96 verts / ~172 tris is low-poly by design (the vendor's own low-poly default)

ranking.rationale: Wins every criterion that matters: (1) D1 - real vendor CC0 eye geometry fitted through MPFB's own ClothesService and the k-NN projection already proven on this rail, not a hand-authored sphere; (2) licence - CC0 verified by reading the asset's own header with named copyright holders, exactly what the brief demands (no 267 MB pack, no pack-page licence claim); (3) pre-strip - deterministic, fits the existing ordered materializer; (4) gaze - inherits the shipped body's measured eye-bone socket weights; (5) effort - smallest acquisition, reuses in-tree proven code.

Same geometry class and same services as C but strictly worse on acquisition: 267 MB pack-level (not header-level) licence claim, pack-install plumbing, and whole-pack sweep. A is effectively C after paying for 1000x more download and a pack-format detour. Falls back here only if the upstream repo host is unreachable and the pack host is not.

Clean licence and guaranteed gaze, but it is the one the brief itself flags: closest to hand-authoring (D1 tension) and a sphere is not an eye. The in-tree precedent (add_mpfb2_eye_rig.py) is an explicit cagematch stage, not a shipped rail. Only if both CC0 eye acquisitions fail AND a measured dead end is recorded for each.

fallbackPolicy: On rank-1 failure: record the measured cause (which contract clause / which gate), then rank-2. On rank-2 failure: rank-3. A measured dead end is a deliverable; no fabricated win.
